title: Deployment updates
summary: Recover stale tabs when production deployments replace routes and hashed assets.

sections.title: Production build checks
sections.body: Use deploymentPlugin with watchDeployment to recover long-lived browser tabs after a deployment. The plugin emits smolter-manifest.json with a unique build version and provides virtual:smolter/deployment. Development and server builds export null, so no update requests run in development or SSR. This is separate from Vite’s asset manifest: it detects replacement builds, including changed routes and hashed bundles.

sections.title: Connect the browser router
sections.body: Connect once before starting a manually created router, or pass deployment metadata directly to mountApplication so recovery also covers the initial route import. Import from /react/client or /preact/client. The helper wraps navigation and Back/Forward, checks a fresh manifest before changing pathname or search, and reloads the intended destination when its version differs. Hash-only changes and external navigations do not check. router.dispose() removes the listeners; the returned cleanup function can disconnect them earlier. No polling runs in the background.

sections.title: Serve production documents and manifests fresh
sections.body: Serve smolter-manifest.json from the same deployed release as its HTML and assets. Set Cache-Control: no-store on the manifest and no-cache on HTML; keep content-hashed assets immutable. Install this route before SPA/SSR fallbacks and generic static-file middleware. The browser also uses fetch cache: no-store. If your CDN ignores these headers, configure its cache rules explicitly. Keep old assets during rollout when possible: the guard cannot run if the initial JavaScript entry itself is missing.

sections.title: Bases, CDNs and multiple applications
sections.body: By default the public manifest URL uses Vite base. Set manifestURL explicitly for a relative base, a reverse proxy or multiple applications sharing a domain. Each application must read its own manifest. The emitted filename remains smolter-manifest.json; your server maps the public URL to that file. Cross-origin asset hosts must allow CORS for manifest reads. Packaged/offline applications can omit the plugin and helper.

sections.title: Failures, forms and reload loops
sections.body: Failed, invalid or timed-out checks continue normal navigation; the default timeout is 2000 ms. The helper never submits or replays mutations. Vite chunk-load failures trigger another version check, but only a confirmed newer build permits recovery, and recovery is skipped while the router is submitting. A sessionStorage marker permits at most one reload per old build and manifest URL. If storage is blocked or the same stale HTML survives a reload, normal errors remain visible instead of creating a reload loop. Unsaved in-memory state is lost on document reload; supply reload(destination) to implement your own confirmation policy. A deployment rolled out across inconsistent servers still requires a consistent host/CDN deployment policy. Idle intent-prefetch failures do not reload the current page or consume the recovery marker. Recovery waits for navigation to record a destination; overlapping checks honor the newest navigation. New history operations invalidate pending checks even when returning to the current route. Starting a mutation cancels earlier recovery checks. Redirect chunk recovery uses the committed router URL, including query and hash, rather than the URL of the original click.

sections.title: Type the virtual module
sections.body: Include this declaration in the application TypeScript project. No physical deployment module needs to be created.
